subject: dsa
title: Trapping Rain Water
summary: Two pointers from both ends. The shorter wall bounds the water, so always advance it; the water over a bar is the tallest wall seen behind it minus its own height.
problem: Each value is a wall height. Compute how much rain water is trapped between the walls.

steps.caption: Each bar is a wall. Rain pools in the dips. How much water is trapped in total?
Two pointers at the ends. Water over a bar = (the shorter of the tallest walls on each side) minus its own height.
Left wall (4) is shorter than right (5), so the left bounds the water. Tallest-on-left = 4; over index 0: 4 - 4 = 0. Move L in.
Tallest-on-left stays 4. Over index 1: 4 - 2 = 2 trapped. Running total: 2. Left is shorter, so move L.
Over index 2: 4 - 0 = 4 trapped. Total: 6. Move L.
Over index 3: 4 - 3 = 1 trapped. Total: 7. Move L.
Over index 4: 4 - 2 = 2 trapped. Total: 9. Move L.
L meets R. Total trapped water = 2 + 4 + 1 + 2 = 9.
